original_text: Seed Development During the globular stage, the proembryo is a ball of cells The outermost cells will become dermal tissue Heart and Torpedo Stages The embryo is heart shaped when cotyledonsappear The embryo enlarges, elongates, and takes on a torpedo shape Mature Embryo The epicotylis the portion between cotyledons contributing to shoot development The hypocotylis the portion below that contributes to stem development The radicleis the embryonic root
explanation: The developing eudicot embryo transitions through several stages: 1) Globular stage: the proembryo is a ball of cells, and its outer layer is destined to differentiate into dermal tissue. 2) Heart stage: the embryo becomes heart-shaped as two cotyledons emerge. 3) Torpedo stage: the embryo enlarges and elongates. 4) Mature embryo: exhibits defined structures: the epicotyl (the region above cotyledon attachment that develops into the shoot), the hypocotyl (the region below cotyledon attachment that contributes to stem development), and the radicle (the embryonic root).

questions.q: Which embryonic region is responsible for developing into the root of the plant?
questions.exp: The radicle is the embryonic root of the plant.

questions.q: What is the developmental sequence of stages for a eudicot embryo?
questions.exp: The embryo develops from a globular stage (ball of cells) to a heart stage (cotyledons appear), then elongates into a torpedo shape, and finally becomes a mature embryo.

questions.q: What will the outermost cells of the globular stage proembryo become?
questions.exp: During the globular stage, the outermost cells of the proembryo are determined to develop into dermal tissue.
